beats.text: Start to surrender in about 38 minutes.
beats.note: 27 August 1896, between the British Empire and the island sultanate of Zanzibar. The whole conflict was over before an hour had passed.

beats.name: Khalid bin Barghash
beats.role: He seized the throne when the pro-British sultan died suddenly. Britain ordered him out by 9am on 27 August. He refused, and barricaded the palace with some 3,000 men.

beats.note: Within two minutes most of Khalid's guns were wrecked and he had slipped out a back door. The shelling did the rest.

beats.context: The length of the war by the usual count; a few sources say closer to 40. Either way, long enough to leave the palace in rubble.

beats.text: About 500 hit on one side. One on the other.
beats.note: Over 500 of Khalid's men were killed or wounded. The only British casualty was a single petty officer: injured, and he recovered.

beats.line: The shortest war in history, and it wasn't close.
